faqs.q: How do I create a Seedance 2.5 Flash video?
faqs.a: Select Flash in the workspace, choose Create, Modify or Extend and supply the inputs requested by that mode. Review the current quote before confirming.
Up to 10 images, 5 videos and 5 audio clips, within the selected mode’s limits. Audio references require a visual input. Edit and extension use their own source-video controls.

faqs.q: Does Flash include 1080p, 4K or native Draft/final?
faqs.a: No. Flash outputs 480p or 720p. Standard Seedance 2.5 has its own 1080p and native Draft-to-final workflow. A Flash generation cannot be finalized as a native Draft.

faqs.q: Are these prompts real Flash results?
faqs.a: The Prompt Lab contains editable scene plans. A video example is attributed to Flash only when it was actually generated by that model.

faqs.q: Where can I see the price?
faqs.a: The page shows current quotes for its sample settings. Your final quote is calculated in the workspace from the model, duration, resolution, audio and source inputs.

section.title: How to prompt Seedance 2.5 Flash
section.intro: Give the scene a purpose, then direct its action, camera and sound. Start with this late-night exchange and make it your own.
section.tip: Change one visible choice between variants so you can compare the results.

tabs.label: The intention
tabs.title: The intention
tabs.description: Start with the people and the moment.
tabs.copy: Two people sit opposite each other in a late-night diner. One quietly asks a short question; the other looks up, smiles and pauses before answering. Keep their positions, clothes and the warm window light consistent.

tabs.label: The camera
tabs.title: The camera
tabs.description: Choose one move that follows the emotion.
tabs.copy: Begin on a medium two-shot in the diner. Push in gently during the exchange and settle on the listener’s reaction. Keep both eyelines coherent, with no cut or sudden camera move.

tabs.label: The sound
tabs.title: The sound
tabs.description: Build a soundscape around the dialogue.
tabs.copy: Two distinct, quiet voices in a late-night diner. Soft room tone and rain against the window. Leave a brief silence after the reply. No music.

globalPrinciples: Describe the action in the order it happens.
Use a camera movement that can follow the subject.
Repeat only the visual details that must stay stable.

demo.title: Scene plan — a late-night exchange
demo.prompt: Two people sit opposite each other in a late-night diner. One quietly asks a short question; the other looks up, smiles and pauses before answering. Keep their positions, clothes and the warm window light consistent. Begin on a medium two-shot in the diner. Push in gently during the exchange and settle on the listener’s reaction. Keep both eyelines coherent, with no cut or sudden camera move. Two distinct, quiet voices in a late-night diner. Soft room tone and rain against the window. Leave a brief silence after the reply. No music.
notes: This scene has not been rendered with Flash. Its settings and result remain to be tested.
